rationale: The hypothesis posits that missense variants localized in the conserved MH2 signaling domain of SMAD2 confer a higher risk of progression from aneurysm to acute aortic dissection compared to upstream truncating or null variants. While initial studies identified MH2 missense variants in familial thoracic aortic disease and parallel findings in SMAD3 (LDS3) demonstrate increased major vascular events and earlier dissections for dominant-negative MH2 variants, empirical SMAD2 cohort data do not validate a statistically higher dissection rate for MH2 missense variants over truncating variants. In SMAD2, truncating variants (such as frameshift/nonsense mutations) have also been identified in cohorts presenting with thoracic aortic aneurysm and dissection, and early reports noted that aortic dissection was rare or absent regardless of variant type. Furthermore, several truncating variants manifest primarily as congenital heart defects (CHD) with laterality defects rather than pure vascular dissection phenotypes, making a definitive assertion of differential dissection risk across variant types unresolved and conflicted by limited sample sizes.

evidence.text: In a cohort of LDS patients with thoracic aneurysms and dissections, SMAD2 truncating mutation c.593dupA was identified in a patient presenting within the cardiovascular disease spectrum, showing that truncating alleles also contribute to severe thoracic aortopathy rather than solely non-dissecting phenotypes.

evidence.text: Analysis of SMAD2 variants revealed two distinct phenotypic manifestations: truncating variants frequently presented with complex congenital heart disease (CHD) with or without laterality defects and developmental delay, while an adult with a predicted deleterious missense variant presented with late-onset vascular aneurysm, supporting domain- and class-specific genotype-phenotype divergence.

source.title: Variable cardiovascular phenotypes associated with SMAD2 pathogenic variants
source.quote: Our data suggest two distinct phenotypes associated with pathogenic variants in SMAD2: complex CHD with or without laterality defects and other congenital anomalies, and a late-onset vascular phenotype characterized by arterial aneurysms with connective tissue abnormalities.

evidence.text: In homologous SMAD3-associated LDS (LDS3), individuals with dominant-negative missense variants in the MH2 domain had significantly more major vascular events occurring at a younger median age compared to those with haploinsufficient variants, illustrating the biological precedent for MH2 missense dominant-negative pathogenicity.

conflicts: Aortic dissection has been documented in carriers of truncating SMAD2 mutations (e.g., c.593dupA), contradicting the hypothesis that dissection risk is exclusively elevated in or restricted to MH2 missense variants.

Earlier SMAD2 cohorts noted a general absence or extreme rarity of acute aortic dissection across all mutation types compared to LDS types 1-4, obscuring definitive statistical separation between missense and truncating dissection rates.

new_directions.question_text: Does an international multi-center registry of SMAD2 variant carriers show a statistically significant hazard ratio for acute aortic dissection in MH2 domain missense versus loss-of-function variants after adjusting for aortic diameter and blood pressure?
new_directions.rationale: Currently described SMAD2 cohorts remain too small (<50 total reported probands) to establish reliable incidence rates of dissection stratified by variant type and functional domain.

new_directions.question_text: Do patient-derived smooth muscle cells carrying MH2 missense SMAD2 variants exhibit dominant-negative disruption of heteromeric transcriptional complexes compared to heterozygous null cell lines?
new_directions.rationale: Establishing whether MH2 variants act via true dominant-negative mechanisms versus haploinsufficiency will clarify the biomechanical basis of vascular wall breakdown and dissection propensity in LDS6.
